title: Sound spreads in three dimensions
hook: Change distance from the source and predict intensity.
misconception: intensity doubles when distance from the source doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply I = P/(4πr²) to compare intensity when distance from the source changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an isotropic point source in a lossless medium with fixed power, I = P/(4πr²). When distance from the source doubles, intensity becomes ¼ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model I = P/(4πr²); scaling exponent -2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an isotropic point source in a lossless medium with fixed power, with a nonzero initial result. If distance from the source triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on intensity?
recall.why: Apply I = P/(4πr²) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/9.
